title: territorial community as a subject of strategic planning of territorial development

original_source.central_claim: A united territorial community is a capable collective actor for socio-economic management, requiring integrated long-term strategic planning.; An analysis–planning–implementation process with stakeholder participation, risk-aware projects and monitoring provides a framework for community development.; Economic and budget development, infrastructure improvement and cultural activity are proposed priority directions; these recommendations are conceptual, not evaluated interventions.

central_claims: A united territorial community is a capable collective actor for socio-economic management, requiring integrated long-term strategic planning.
An analysis–planning–implementation process with stakeholder participation, risk-aware projects and monitoring provides a framework for community development.
Economic and budget development, infrastructure improvement and cultural activity are proposed priority directions; these recommendations are conceptual, not evaluated interventions.

source_manifest.title: United territorial community as a subject of strategic planning of territorial development
source_manifest.finding: Conceptual review proposes integrated planning, participation and risk-aware project monitoring; it reports no evaluated intervention.

source_manifest.title: The Potential of Territorial Communities as a Factor of Socio-Environmental Development of Territories
source_manifest.finding: Independent comparative synthesis expressly takes the article into account and adopts its resource-capacity interpretation in discussion; European examples do not implement its particular planning scheme.

source_manifest.title: Development of international cooperation of the borderline territorial communities of Ukraine with the EU countries under martial law
source_manifest.finding: Lyndyuk and colleagues survey border communities and cite the target only among background decentralization studies; the survey is not an evaluation of its planning process.

source_manifest.title: Territorial Community as a Primary Subject of Security-oriented Development of Critical Infrastructure of the Territory
source_manifest.finding: Later work concerns community planning but its abstract and references do not connect its influence-contour model to the assigned paper.

answers.rationale: No independent primary study explicitly validates the proposed integrated planning process; the 2023 survey studies international cooperation under martial law.
No independent reconstruction or evaluation of the analysis–planning–implementation scheme was found.
The border-community survey does not test the original recommendations, despite collecting new data.
Later authors accept the community-capacity definition, but no authoritative assessment explicitly evaluates the complete recorded planning claims.
The original discusses weak capacity, participation and risk management; no follow-up directly tests whether its approach survives these limitations.
Later socio-environmental and international-cooperation work acknowledges the target, but a substantive extension of its specific planning scheme was not demonstrated.
Two citing teams were identified, but citation and shared subject matter do not establish two substantive builders.
The 2023 synthesis uses the capacity interpretation in discussion without actually implementing the proposed planning process.
No read review identifies this article as enabling a new line of research.
No independent benchmark against another planning process was verified.
European community successes in the later synthesis are not attributed to applying this paper’s scheme.
No documented application of its specific process to another community was established.
The later survey and environmental case discussion were not shown to be enabled by this specific scheme.
Actual municipal use of strategic planning is common in the sources, but adoption traceable to this article was not documented.
No fair evaluation compares the suggested integrated scheme with alternatives on effectiveness or cost.
The substantive conceptual acknowledgment is from 2023, less than three years later; the 2026 related article does not establish use of this paper.
No verified positive assessment after the three-year anniversary specifically evaluates this contribution.
The two verified citing studies are both from 2023; another year of substantive follow-up was not established.

An independent comparative research synthesis adopts the article’s community-capacity concept as part of its socio-environmental interpretation, without establishing the effectiveness of the planning recommendations.

evidence.explanation: Literature review identifies target reference 9; discussion uses its accumulation-and-use-of-resources conception.

answers.rationale: No comparison with newer approaches explicitly demonstrates continued usefulness of the proposed process.

search_gaps: Published English full text read; some translation is awkward but the proposed process and conclusions are identifiable.
No independent intervention evaluation or municipal implementation record traceable to this article was verified.
Lifetime observation through 2026-09-16; the assigned pilot sample is not an unbiased estimate of all research outcomes.
research.summary: Independent conceptual uptake is documented in a 2023 synthesis. Actual implementation, causal benefits and validation of this particular planning process remain unknown.
